free_tier.stated: No consumer-facing capacity. Quoted: 'RL Swarm is a peer-to-peer reinforcement-learning swarm you can run on a laptop or a GPU server', with system requirements 'A 64-bit arm64 or x86 CPU with at least 32 GB RAM, or an officially supported NVIDIA GPU (3090, 4090, 5090, A100, H100)'. The dashboard states: 'There are no official swarms running right now.'

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: None. Gensyn is a market for selling compute, not buying it, and it has no live swarm. A chain that includes Gensyn would need a GPU already in place.

limits.value: The direction is inverted: Gensyn pays suppliers who bring hardware, so it consumes hardware rather than supplying it. Even as a supplier lane it fails first on the 32 GB RAM or supported-GPU floor, then on 'no official swarms running right now'.

identity_cost.detail: a Hugging Face write token: the getting-started page is quoted as requiring 'a Hugging Face write token', which in turn implies a Hugging Face account that issues it. No card, hold, phone or ID is stated, and the email kind rests on that Hugging Face account rather than on a quoted signup form. Debit and prepaid do not arise because no payment method is mentioned. The 32 GB RAM or listed NVIDIA GPU requirement is a capacity gate, not an identity one.

evidence.proved: quoted: requires a 64-bit arm64/x86 CPU with at least 32 GB RAM or a supported NVIDIA GPU (3090, 4090, 5090, A100, H100); a Hugging Face write token is required
quoted: 'There are no official swarms running right now. Please check back later'; the network reports 427,530 on-chain users
public testnet launched March 2025; the network tracks participation and makes payments, it does not rent capacity to consumers
third-party operator guide states 'No compute-provider earnings have been published for Gensyn mainnet' and that testnet rewards were 'relative and pool-based'

record.notes: REFUTATION OF A COMMON MISREADING. Gensyn appears in free-GPU roundups because RL Swarm is free to join, but joining means contributing hardware, not receiving capacity. Three independent facts kill it as a source of capacity: it needs 32 GB RAM or a listed NVIDIA card, its dashboard says no official swarms are running, and its reward unit is a token allocation out of a 2 percent testnet pool with no published per-node formula. A third-party guide also records that renting a GPU to run a Gensyn node costs USD 65 to USD 300 per month.
